scene: Dense night market: crowd, shops, lanterns and continuous walking motion
selection: User selected the James Lo crowded night-market reference before any outputs were generated; evaluated for dense scene detail and multi-person motion.
scope: Four matching clips; QAD cuDNN and QAD Sage newly generated as a pair; BF16/Online retained from v1.31.
requested_actions: Wide crowded street, slow forward movement, independent pedestrians and a shopping-bag handoff; prompt targets must be distinguished from observed behavior.

visual_review.scope: Visual contact-sheet review at frames 0,24,48,72,96,120; full-video similarity measured separately.

retained_BF16_Online_review.method: Visual inspection of decoded frames 0, 24, 48, 72, 96 and 120 for all three outputs.
retained_BF16_Online_review.observed: All three retain a densely populated night-market wide composition, shopfronts and overhead lanterns. Foreground pedestrians move through and occlude the crowd; positions and appearances diverge between variants.
retained_BF16_Online_review.not_verified: The prompt requested a shopping-bag handoff and a one-metre camera glide; neither is asserted as successfully realized.

new_QAD_and_Sage: Dense crowd, shops, lantern strings and the wide night-market composition persist in both clips.
Foreground pedestrians change position and occlude others; the two clips differ in individual appearance and motion.
No whole-frame corruption or blank frames was apparent in the sampled frames.
Small-face and text fidelity, action correctness and temporal stability are not established by this sampled visual check.

timing_limitations: One first request per fresh model process with shared GEMM/Sage JIT cache populated; no full-model warmup. The initial QAD cold-compile request is retained separately and excluded from displayed timing.
Both new QAD variants ran on physical GPU 3 with the same isolated runtime and FlashInfer source; Sage ran before the displayed warm-cache QAD repeat. Other GPUs had unrelated workloads.
BF16 and direct Online NVFP4 are retained from v1.31 on GPU 0 of the same machine; cross-arm request times are not a controlled production speed benchmark.
Single-GPU layerwise CPU offload; one sample does not establish steady-state SageAttention speedup.

sage_attention.linears: Same published QAD NVFP4 DiT checkpoint as QAD control
sage_attention.fine_attention: CAKE Sage via FlashInfer: INT8 Q/K and FP8 V, BF16 output
sage_attention.routing: Logical tile128 and sparsity0.9 retained; exact mask expansion to 64-token compute tiles; pooling, top-k, dense prefix and learned coarse correction unchanged
sage_attention.token_refiner: Same BF16 SDPA fallback as other arms
sage_attention.runtime_overlay: Two guards in isolated runtime enable existing tile128 mask adapter for Sage; see sage-tile128-dispatch.patch

correction: The QAD clips used dynamic activation globals instead of checkpoint globals, with non-native attention/encoder/decoder precision. See the corrected v1.34 comparison.
